key_insight: For intermetallic NRR catalysts, s- and p-band descriptors can outperform the traditional d-band center in predicting adsorption, revealing a broader electronic design space.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, low-cost ML descriptor set for screening non-noble catalysts for ammonia synthesis with DFT-level insight and reduced computation.
method: Built a high-throughput DFT dataset for 47 bimetallic intermetallic compounds (~1,200 adsorption energies).
Trained ML models using intrinsic material properties, band centers/fillings, and local Bader-charge features.
Used SHAP analysis to identify the most influential descriptors for N2, N2H, and NH3 adsorption.
evidence_signal: The models achieved MAEs of 0.26 eV for N2, 0.39 eV for N2H, and 0.17 eV for NH3 adsorption using only 20 key features.
watch_item: The descriptor importance is inferred from a specific 47-IMC dataset, so transferability to other alloy families or surface chemistries should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: Going Beyond the d-band Center to Design Intermetallic Catalysts for Nitrogen Reduction: A High-Throughput DFT and Machine Learning Study
